source.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix

teaching.hint: For a proposed value, can the two sorted directions help count how many entries do not exceed it?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The count of values at most a threshold can be found by a monotone staircase, allowing a search for the first threshold whose rank reaches k.
solution_outline.approach: Search the value range from the smallest to largest matrix entries. At each trial, sweep a staircase boundary through rows and columns to count entries no larger than the trial value.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The staircase count is exact and nondecreasing with the trial value; the search keeps a threshold below rank k and one at or above it.
solution_outline.correctness: The first value with at least k entries below or equal is precisely the kth entry, including duplicates. The staircase visits at most two sides of the matrix per count.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n log V) time for numeric range V and O(1) auxiliary space; compute midpoints in wide arithmetic.
solution_outline.pitfall: Counting distinct values instead of entries gives the wrong rank when duplicates occur.

common_wrong_turns: Flatten and sort using quadratic extra storage
Use a 32-bit sum for extreme midpoint values
source_fidelity_notes: The nondecreasing row and column rules, duplicate ranking, and memory requirement are explicit.
